object_types: site type: island settlement and tombs;tomb;pottery

name: Sumhuram
making_significance: Sumhuram was a walled port exporting frankincense by sea to India and the Red Sea.

name: Aden
making_significance: Aden was a transit port whose merchants appear in Cairo Geniza letters handling Indian textiles, pepper and metals.

name: Mocha
making_significance: Mocha was the main export port for Yemeni coffee until plantations elsewhere replaced it.

name: Kiswa factory
making_significance: The factory weaves and embroiders the black silk cover for the Kaaba each year, work long done in Cairo.

name: Louvre Abu Dhabi
making_significance: The museum, built under a 2007 agreement with France, arranges works from many cultures in one chronological 'universal' sequence.
defined_by: the Abu Dhabi government; Agence France-Muséums
leaves_out: the migrant workers who built it

name: Muharraq pearling sites
making_significance: Pearling from Muharraq relied on divers held in debt to boat captains and merchants until cultured pearls ended the trade.
object_types: site type: pearling town and oyster beds;pearl
leaves_out: the divers, many of them in debt bondage or enslaved
free_sources: Wikimedia Commons;Qatar Digital Library (open licence to verify)

name: Göbekli Tepe
making_significance: Hunter-gatherers carved T-shaped limestone pillars with animal reliefs for monumental enclosures before farming was established.

name: Çatalhöyük
making_significance: Houses at Çatalhöyük had wall paintings, plaster reliefs and burials under floors, and obsidian was ground into mirrors.

name: Göllü Dağ
making_significance: Obsidian from Göllü Dağ, knapped at workshops on the volcano, was carried to the Levant and Cyprus.
object_types: site type: obsidian source and workshops;blade;core

name: Kültepe
making_significance: Tens of thousands of letters found in Kaneš's merchant quarter record Assyrian traders exchanging tin and woollen textiles for silver.
leaves_out: the women in Assur who wove the textiles

name: Uluburun shipwreck
making_significance: A Late Bronze Age ship sank carrying copper and tin ingots, glass ingots, ivory and ebony.

name: Sardis
making_significance: Excavations found the Lydian gold refinery that separated gold from silver for early coinage.

name: Iznik
making_significance: Iznik potters made fritware painted under the glaze, supplying tiles for Ottoman mosques and palaces.
free_sources: Met Open Access (CC0);Cleveland Museum of Art Open Access (CC0);Wikimedia Commons

name: Bursa
making_significance: Bursa's silk market and looms made the city the centre of Ottoman silk weaving and trade with Iran.
object_types: site type: silk market and caravanserai;velvet;kaftan

name: Grand Bazaar
making_significance: Mehmed II's covered market grew into a district of shops and workshops for textiles, jewellery and metalwork.

name: Dmanisi
making_significance: Oldowan tools and hominin fossils about 1.8 million years old are among the earliest outside Africa.

name: Dzudzuana Cave
making_significance: Flax fibres from Dzudzuana, some dyed and twisted, suggest cord or textile making over 30,000 years ago.

name: Areni-1
making_significance: The cave preserved a leather shoe about 5,500 years old and a wine-pressing installation.

name: Gadachrili Gora
making_significance: Jar residues from Gadachrili Gora are among the earliest chemical evidence of grape wine.

name: Kubachi
making_significance: Kubachi's metalworkers make engraved silver and weapons, and Iranian pottery kept in its houses was misnamed 'Kubachi ware' by collectors.
object_types: site type: mountain craft village;engraved silver;dagger

name: Matenadaran
other_names: Mesrop Mashtots Institute of Ancient Manuscripts, Yerevan, Armenia
making_significance: The manuscript repository keeps Armenian illuminated manuscripts gathered from monasteries and scriptoria.

name: Knossos
making_significance: The Minoan palace had workshops and storerooms recorded in Linear B, and Arthur Evans's concrete reconstructions still shape how it is seen.
leaves_out: the Cretan workmen and restorers

name: Kerameikos
making_significance: The potters' quarter of Athens and its cemetery give painted pottery, including large Geometric grave markers, together with the graves they stood on.
object_types: site type: potters' quarter and cemetery;amphora;lekythos
leaves_out: enslaved and metic workers in the potteries

name: Laurion
making_significance: Enslaved miners dug the silver of Laurion, which paid for Athens's fleet from 483 BCE and its owl coinage.
leaves_out: the enslaved miners

name: Workshop of Pheidias
making_significance: Excavators found moulds and tools for the gold-and-ivory statue of Zeus and a cup inscribed 'I belong to Pheidias'.
leaves_out: the workshop's assistants

name: Delos
making_significance: As a Roman-era free port Delos became a large market for enslaved people and for goods traded across the eastern Mediterranean.
object_types: site type: island port and market;mosaic

name: Arretine workshops
making_significance: Arezzo's workshops made mould-decorated red-gloss tableware stamped with the names of owners and slave workers.
object_types: site type: pottery workshops;sigillata bowl;potter's stamp
leaves_out: the enslaved potters named on stamps
notes: Workers such as those of Perennius and Ateius signed stamps.

name: Pompeii
making_significance: The buried town preserves fulleries, bakeries and workshops alongside houses and the bodies of victims.
object_types: site type: buried town with workshops;fresco;bronze;oven
leaves_out: the enslaved workforce of households and workshops

name: Carrara marble quarries
making_significance: Marble from the quarries above Carrara was used from Roman times through Michelangelo to present-day extraction.
leaves_out: quarry workers killed in accidents

name: Banditaccia necropolis
making_significance: Etruscan tombs at Cerveteri were looted for vases, including the Euphronios krater sold to the Met in 1972 and returned to Italy in 2008.

name: Constantinople
making_significance: Imperial workshops in Constantinople made silk, ivories and enamels under guild rules set in the Book of the Eparch.
object_types: site type: imperial capital and workshops;silk textile;ivory;enamel
free_sources: Met Open Access (CC0);Cleveland Museum of Art Open Access (CC0);Wikimedia Commons

name: Varna Necropolis
making_significance: Graves at Varna held some of the earliest worked gold objects, with copper and shell.

name: Rudna Glava
making_significance: Vinča-period miners sank shafts into copper ore at Rudna Glava.

name: Belovode
making_significance: Slag from Belovode is among the earliest known evidence of copper smelting.

name: Mount Athos
making_significance: Monasteries on Athos keep icon, manuscript and woodcarving workshops and libraries of Byzantine material.
leaves_out: women, barred from the peninsula

name: Chauvet Cave
date_note: approx.; two phases c. 37,000-33,500 and 31,000-28,000 cal BP
making_significance: Charcoal and ochre paintings of lions, horses and rhinoceroses in Chauvet are among the oldest known figurative cave art, now closed and shown by a replica.

name: Lascaux
making_significance: Painted and engraved animals at Lascaux were closed to the public in 1963 and are shown through successive replicas.

name: Dolní Věstonice
making_significance: Gravettian hunters fired clay figurines, including the 'Venus' of Dolní Věstonice, in hearths long before pottery.

name: Hohle Fels
making_significance: Hohle Fels yielded a mammoth-ivory female figurine and a bone flute about 40,000 years old.

name: Hallstatt salt mine
making_significance: Salt preserved Bronze and Iron Age miners' tools, textiles and leather in Hallstatt's mine beside a rich cemetery.
object_types: site type: salt mine and cemetery;textile;carrying pack

name: La Graufesenque
making_significance: Firing lists scratched on plates name the potters sharing each kiln load of samian ware that went across the Roman west.
object_types: site type: pottery workshops;samian bowl;firing list
leaves_out: the potters named in the lists

name: Rialto
making_significance: The Rialto market and nearby fondaci linked Venice's trade with Byzantium, Egypt and the Levant to its crafts.
object_types: site type: market and trading houses;textile;glass

name: Murano
making_significance: Venice's glassmakers were concentrated on Murano, where clear cristallo and later techniques were developed under guild control.

name: Genoa
making_significance: Genoa's merchants ran Black Sea and Mediterranean trade, including in enslaved people from the Black Sea, and banked the Spanish Crown.
leaves_out: enslaved people from the Black Sea

name: Albrechtsburg porcelain factory
making_significance: Meissen made the earliest European hard-paste porcelain, building on Böttger and Tschirnhaus's experiments.
defined_by: Augustus the Strong; J. F. Böttger
leaves_out: the modellers and painters

name: Sèvres
making_significance: The royal porcelain manufactory made soft-paste and later hard-paste porcelain for the French court.

name: Gobelins
making_significance: Colbert's royal manufactory brought tapestry and furniture makers together under Charles Le Brun.
leaves_out: Flemish weavers recruited to Paris

name: Aubusson
making_significance: Low-warp tapestry workshops in Aubusson were made royal manufactories in 1665 and revived by Jean Lurçat from 1939.
leaves_out: the weavers behind named designers
notes: UNESCO Representative List of the Intangible Cultural Heritage 2009 ("Aubusson tapestry"), verified.

name: Bauhaus Dessau
making_significance: Gropius's school building housed workshops for furniture, textiles and metal whose products were licensed to industry.
object_types: site type: school building and workshops;chair;textile;lamp
leaves_out: women weavers steered into the weaving workshop

name: Bauhaus Weimar
making_significance: The Bauhaus began in Henry van de Velde's arts and crafts school buildings in Weimar.

name: HfG Ulm
making_significance: Max Bill's building for the Ulm School of Design housed teaching tied to industry, notably with Braun.
defined_by: Max Bill; Inge Aicher-Scholl; Otl Aicher

name: Champ de Mars
making_significance: The Paris universal expositions on the Champ de Mars displayed industry and colonies side by side, including exhibited villages of colonised people.
leaves_out: the colonised people exhibited

name: Louvre
making_significance: The Louvre filled its galleries with works seized by Napoleon's armies, many of which were returned in 1815.

name: Musée du quai Branly
other_names: Musée du quai Branly-Jacques Chirac, Paris, France
making_significance: The museum gathered colonial-era collections of African, Oceanian, Asian and American objects, and returned 26 Abomey objects to Benin in 2021.

name: Humboldt Forum
making_significance: The rebuilt palace houses Berlin's ethnological and Asian art collections, and Germany transferred ownership of its Benin bronzes to Nigeria in 2022.

name: Great Orme mines
making_significance: Bronze Age miners dug kilometres of tunnels with bone and stone tools to reach copper ore.

name: Grime's Graves
making_significance: Neolithic miners sank hundreds of shafts to reach high-quality flint for axes.

name: Sutton Hoo
making_significance: The Mound 1 ship burial held gold and garnet fittings, a helmet and imported silver.

name: Bruges
making_significance: Bruges was a cloth town and trading hub where Hanseatic, Italian and Iberian merchants met.

name: Antwerp
making_significance: Sixteenth-century Antwerp's bourse, printers and painters' guild made it a market for spices, paintings and books.

name: Amsterdam
making_significance: Amsterdam was the seat of the VOC and WIC and a market for Asian goods, sugar and the trade in enslaved Africans.
object_types: site type: port and exchange;ship;export goods

name: Delft potteries
making_significance: Delft potters made tin-glazed earthenware imitating Chinese blue-and-white when Chinese supply fell after 1644.

name: Stoke-on-Trent
making_significance: Stoke's bottle-oven works made earthenware and bone china for world markets, with children employed in many tasks.
leaves_out: children and women workers

name: Etruria Works
making_significance: Josiah Wedgwood's factory divided work into specialist tasks and made jasperware and the 1787 anti-slavery medallion.
leaves_out: the workers and modellers

name: Coalbrookdale
making_significance: Abraham Darby smelted iron with coke at Coalbrookdale in 1709, and the nearby Iron Bridge was cast there in 1779.

name: Soho Manufactory
making_significance: Matthew Boulton's works gathered button-making, silver plate and ormolu under one roof and was linked to Boulton and Watt's engines.

name: Ancoats
making_significance: Steam-powered cotton mills in Ancoats spun cotton grown largely by enslaved people in the American South.
leaves_out: the enslaved cotton growers; child workers

name: Liverpool
making_significance: Liverpool's ships carried a large share of the British trade in enslaved Africans, loaded with textiles and metal goods for Africa.

name: Crystal Palace
making_significance: Joseph Paxton's prefabricated iron-and-glass hall housed the Great Exhibition, which ranked the goods of nations and colonies.
defined_by: the Royal Commission; Prince Albert; Henry Cole
leaves_out: the builders and the colonial makers of exhibits

name: British Museum
making_significance: The museum's collections, from Sloane's founding bequest to Benin and Maqdala, are at the centre of restitution debates.

name: South Kensington Museum
making_significance: Founded after the Great Exhibition to improve design, the museum collected decorative arts as models for industry.

name: Pitt Rivers Museum
making_significance: The museum arranges objects by type rather than place, following Augustus Pitt Rivers's evolutionary ideas, and removed human remains from display in 2020.
defined_by: Augustus Pitt Rivers; University of Oxford

name: Altamira
making_significance: Polychrome bison at Altamira were dismissed as fakes after their 1879 discovery until Paleolithic art was accepted in 1902.
leaves_out: María Sanz de Sautuola, credited with first seeing the paintings

name: Lagar Velho
making_significance: The burial of a child with ochre and a shell pendant is one of the best-studied Gravettian burials in Iberia.

name: Rio Tinto
making_significance: Copper and silver have been mined at Rio Tinto from prehistory through Rome to the company founded in 1873.
leaves_out: the miners and their 1888 protest

name: Almadén
making_significance: Almadén's mercury, mined partly by convicts and enslaved people, was shipped to the Americas to refine silver.
leaves_out: convict and enslaved miners

name: Madinat al-Zahra
making_significance: The caliphal palace city had workshops for carved ivory boxes, marble and textiles.

name: Seville
making_significance: Seville held the royal monopoly on trade with the Americas, and its Triana potters made tiles for both sides of the Atlantic.
leaves_out: enslaved Africans in the city

name: Lisbon
making_significance: Lisbon received Asian and African goods and enslaved Africans through the Casa da Índia until the 1755 earthquake.

name: Talavera de la Reina
making_significance: Talavera's tin-glazed potters supplied tiles and wares that gave their name to Mexican talavera.

name: Manises
making_significance: Manises potters made lustreware exported across Europe, including to Italian patrons.

name: Sungir
making_significance: Burials at Sungir held thousands of mammoth-ivory beads sewn on clothing.

name: Nerev End
making_significance: Excavations here found birch-bark letters and workshops of leatherworkers and jewellers.

name: Kremlin Armoury
making_significance: The tsars' workshops made arms, icons, goldwork and textiles, including work by Simon Ushakov.

name: Imperial Porcelain Factory
making_significance: The factory made court porcelain and after 1917 painted agitprop designs on its stock.

name: Vkhutemas building
making_significance: The Higher Art and Technical Studios taught Constructivist design here.

name: Wieliczka Salt Mine
making_significance: Miners at Wieliczka carved chapels and statues out of rock salt.

name: Magnitogorsk
making_significance: The Soviet steel city was built from 1929 largely by deported peasants and prisoners.
leaves_out: the deported and imprisoned labourers

name: Birka
making_significance: Graves at Birka held silks and silver from far away, and workshops made beads and combs.
object_types: site type: trading town and cemetery;bead;comb;silk

name: Hedeby
making_significance: Hedeby's workshops made glass beads, combs and metalwork in a trading town between the Baltic and North Sea.

name: Oseberg ship burial
making_significance: The ship burial of two women held a carved cart and sleighs, looms and tapestry fragments.

name: Falun Mine
making_significance: Copper from Falun funded Sweden's empire, and its by-product became the red paint on Swedish wooden houses.

name: Bryggen
making_significance: Hanseatic merchants at Bryggen traded stockfish for grain and goods, and runic sticks found there record everyday messages.
object_types: site type: wharf and trading houses;runic stick

name: Jokkmokk winter market
making_significance: Sámi makers sell duodji at the market, which the Swedish crown set up to collect taxes.

name: Kiruna
making_significance: Iron-ore mining at Kiruna now requires moving the town and conflicts with Sámi reindeer herding.
leaves_out: Sámi reindeer herders

name: Madjedbebe
date_note: approx.; c. 65,000 years (Clarkson et al. 2017), contested
making_significance: Ground-edge axe fragments, grindstones and ochre from Madjedbebe are dated by the excavators to around 65,000 years ago, a date other archaeologists contest.

name: Carpenter's Gap
making_significance: A fragment of a ground-edge axe from Carpenter's Gap is dated to about 45,000-49,000 years ago.

name: Nawarla Gabarnmang
making_significance: Jawoyn rock shelter with a painted ceiling, a charcoal drawing about 28,000 years old and an early ground-edge axe fragment.

name: Budj Bim
making_significance: The Gunditjmara built channels, weirs and traps in lava flows to farm eels.
object_types: site type: aquaculture landscape;eel trap;stone house

name: Willandra Lakes
making_significance: Mungo Lady and Mungo Man, about 40,000 years old, were taken for study and later returned to their people.
defined_by: the Paakantyi, Mutthi Mutthi and Ngiyampaa; UNESCO

name: Murujuga
making_significance: Murujuga has more than a million rock engravings, now beside heavy industry.

name: Wilgie Mia
date_note: approx.; c. 30,000 years is an estimate from the volume mined (V. Winton), not a scientific date
making_significance: Aboriginal miners dug red and yellow ochre at Wilgie Mia, traded widely.
notes: Start date uncertain: no published dates; National Heritage List (2011) gives none; the 27,000-40,000-year figures in popular sources are unsupported.

name: Mount William
making_significance: Wurundjeri quarried greenstone at Mount William for axes traded across southeast Australia.

name: Juukan Gorge
making_significance: Two rock shelters were blown up by Rio Tinto in 2020 to expand an iron-ore mine.
defined_by: the Puutu Kunti Kurrama and Pinikura

name: Port Arthur
making_significance: Convicts at Port Arthur built ships and made shoes and other goods.

name: Kuk Swamp
making_significance: Mounds and drainage ditches at Kuk show plant cultivation in the New Guinea highlands by about 7,000 years ago, with earlier plant use around 10,000 years ago.

name: Talasea obsidian sources
other_names: Kutau-Bao, Willaumez Peninsula, New Britain, Papua New Guinea
making_significance: Obsidian from Talasea was carried as far as Borneo and Fiji during the Lapita period.

name: Lapita type site
other_names: Site 13, Foué peninsula, Koné, New Caledonia
making_significance: Pottery from the Koné site named the Lapita culture, known for its dentate-stamped designs.

name: Teouma
making_significance: The earliest known cemetery of the first settlers of Vanuatu held dentate-stamped Lapita pots, some used as burial vessels, and headless burials whose skulls were moved.
defined_by: archaeologists (Stuart Bedford; Matthew Spriggs; Vanuatu Cultural Centre)

name: Langa Langa Lagoon
making_significance: Langa Langa makers grind, drill and string small shell discs into shell money still used for bride price and compensation.
object_types: site type: lagoon villages;shell money strand

name: Roi Mata's Domain
making_significance: The residence, death place and burial of the chief Roi Mata remain governed by oral tradition and a tabu kept by local communities.
object_types: site type: chiefly residence and burial site;burial

name: Kiriwina
other_names: Trobriand Islands, Milne Bay, Papua New Guinea
making_significance: Kiriwina's carvers make canoe prow-boards and splashboards for voyages in the kula ring, which exchanges shell necklaces and armbands between islands.
object_types: site type: island villages;canoe prow-board;shell necklace;armband

name: Nan Madol
making_significance: The Saudeleur built nearly a hundred artificial islets of stacked basalt columns and coral fill for chiefly residences and tombs.
object_types: site type: islet ceremonial centre;tomb;stone wall
leaves_out: the labour levied from across Pohnpei

name: Leluh
making_significance: High walls of basalt columns on Leluh island enclosed a chiefly town with compounds, canals and tombs.

name: Yap stone money banks
making_significance: Stone money discs in Yapese village banks change owner without being moved, their history held in shared memory.
object_types: site type: village stone-money bank;stone money disc

name: House of Taga
other_names: San José, Tinian, Northern Mariana Islands
making_significance: The tallest known latte stones, two-part limestone pillars that raised Chamorro buildings, stand at the House of Taga.

name: Bikini Atoll
making_significance: The United States tested 23 nuclear devices at Bikini after removing its people, and those who returned in the 1970s were moved out again in 1978.
leaves_out: the Bikinians
notes: 23 tests at Bikini per UNESCO; World Heritage 2010 (Bikini Atoll Nuclear Test Site).

name: Nauru phosphate fields
making_significance: Phosphate mined for fertiliser by colonial companies, with indentured Chinese and Pacific Islander labour, left most of Nauru's interior stripped.
defined_by: the Pacific Phosphate Company; British Phosphate Commissioners
leaves_out: the Nauruans and indentured miners

name: Taputapuātea
making_significance: Taputapuātea's stone marae were a centre for voyaging chiefs and priests, and it is still a meeting point for canoe revival voyages.

name: Rano Raraku
making_significance: Most of Rapa Nui's moai were carved from the volcanic tuff of Rano Raraku, where hundreds of unfinished figures remain.

name: Orongo
making_significance: The birdman ceremonial village has carved petroglyphs, and the basalt moai Hoa Hakananai'a was taken from it by a British ship's crew in 1868.
notes: Rapanui have asked for its return.

name: Te Papa Tongarewa
making_significance: The national museum is run on a bicultural partnership with Māori and leads the repatriation of Māori and Moriori ancestral remains.
defined_by: the New Zealand state; iwi partners
free_sources: Te Papa Collections Online (CC BY where marked)

name: Bishop Museum
making_significance: Founded in memory of the Hawaiian aliʻi Bernice Pauahi Bishop, the museum holds royal feather cloaks and Pacific collections.

name: Wairau Bar
making_significance: One of the earliest settlements in Aotearoa held stone adzes, moa-egg vessels and burials, whose remains were returned to Rangitāne in 2009.
object_types: site type: settlement and burial ground;adze;necklace

name: Arahura River
other_names: Te Tai Poutini (West Coast), Aotearoa New Zealand
making_significance: The Arahura is a main source of pounamu (nephrite), shaped into adzes and hei-tiki and now owned by Ngāi Tahu.
free_sources: Te Papa Collections Online (CC BY where marked);Auckland Museum Collections Online (CC BY where marked)

name: Keanakākoʻi
making_significance: Hawaiian adze makers worked fine basalt near the summit of Mauna Kea.

name: Nukuleka
making_significance: Nukuleka has some of the earliest dated Lapita pottery in Polynesia.
